existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Basic has no local R4-to-R6 hard structural break, but it does have three material migration risks: a stronger/different `Basic.code` binding, `Basic.created` changing from `date` to `dateTime`, and `Basic.author` adding `Device` and `CareTeam` targets. The top uncertainty is how R4 Basic Resource Types codes should map to R6 version-independent resource type codes.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: R4 Basic instances should usually parse structurally in R6, but terminology conformance and generated model types need attention. Reverse conversion from R6 to R4 is not lossless when R6 uses time-of-day precision in `created` or the new `author` target types. `Basic.code` migration may require a ConceptMap or profile-specific policy because the code is a modifier and drives interpretation of the whole Basic instance.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element identity, cardinality, type, reference-target, and binding-strength deltas because they come directly from local StructureDefinition files. Overall confidence is medium because the most nuanced finding, `Basic.code`, depends on extensible-binding applicability and no official diff, narrative rationale, expansion, or ConceptMap was available locally.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Basic keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 0 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 6/100, producing migration shape `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, major migration `No`, and compatibility posture `preserve-compatibility-per-change`.

recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Treat this as a mostly stable resource. Individual hard breaks, renames, required bindings, or behavior changes should stand or fall on their own rationale and available less-breaking alternatives.

topFindings.title: Basic.code binding changed from example Basic Resource Types to extensible version-independent resource types
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: no JSON shape changed, but the stronger extensible binding can create R6 terminology conformance warnings or local errors for old-only codings when a resource-type code applies; there is also runtime interpretation work for systems that branch on the modifier code.

topFindings.title: Basic.author added Device and CareTeam reference targets
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `author` references to Device or CareTeam are outside R4's targetProfile and search-target lists; all R4 author targets remain valid in R6, so there is no forward old-valid/new-invalid break.
